name: One country, two systems
summary: One country, two systems is the Chinese constitutional principle that a region can be part of the People's Republic while keeping its own economic, legal and social system under a high degree of autonomy. It was devised for Taiwan and first applied to Hong Kong and Macao, with the mainland staying socialist. Its sources insist that sovereignty is indivisible and that the autonomy is delegated by the central government.
scope: The policy as set out in Article 31 of the PRC Constitution, the Hong Kong Basic Law, the Anti-Secession Law and the State Council white papers of 2014 and 2022. It covers the constitutional relationship between the centre and a special region and the offer to Taiwan; it excludes the wider programme of the Chinese Communist Party and Deng Xiaoping's reform policies, so most statements are null.
